newsitem.title: JAPAN: North Korea raps U.S. Secretary of State Albright.
newsitem.headline: North Korea raps U.S. Secretary of State Albright.

text.p: North Korea's official media on Tuesday criticised U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright's recent visits to South Korea and Japan, saying she was trying to isolate and stifle North Korea.

"Albright's trip shows the United States has no intention to settle the issue of the Korean peninsula but is still seeking to isolate and stifle the DPRK (North Korea)," said the Rodon Sinmun, the newspaper of the ruling Korean Workers' Party.
Rodon Sinmun's commentary was carried by the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) which was monitored in Tokyo.
Albright visited Seoul and Tokyo as part of a nine-country tour that ended in Beijing on Tuesday.

In talks with South Korean Foreign Minister Yoo Chong-ha in Seoul, Albright confirmed that North Korea will attend preliminary peace talks on March 5 about ending tension on the divided Korean peninsula.
The commentary made no mention of the preliminary peace talks, called a "briefing", but it said the United States, South Korea and Japan were trying to corner North Korea.

"This time the U.S. talked about a 'consultative meeting to examine the situation of the North', 'proposal for strengthening joint action in the policy towards the North' and 'joint defence'. This is far from the attitude the U.S. should take as a direct party responsible for the settlement of the Korean issue," Rodon Sinmun said.

"The 'cooperation system' called for by the U.S., South Korean puppets and the Japanese reactionaries is a product of their joint plot intended to stifle the DPRK. We have strongly opposed it from the beginning and this stand still remains unchanged," the commentary said.
